data.title: Fabricated Expertise Used to Credential the Claim
data.summary:
Accounts presenting as subject-matter experts — with claimed qualifications, affiliations
or professional history that could not be verified — were used to lend authority to the
campaign's claims.
data.description:
An audience that cannot evaluate a technical claim evaluates the person making it.
Manufacturing a credential is therefore cheaper than manufacturing an argument, and it is
the standard move where the campaign's claim would not survive expert scrutiny.

The credentials are usually checkable and usually fail: the institution has no such
person, the professional body has no such registration, the publication record does not
exist, and the profile photograph appears elsewhere. Where a claimed affiliation is to a
real organisation, that organisation has standing to act and is often willing to.

Record what was checked and what the check returned, including checks that came back
inconclusive. An unverifiable credential is not the same as a disproved one, and the
report should not blur them.
data.recommendation:
* Verify claimed affiliations with the named institution and professional body, and record
  the result of each check including the inconclusive ones.
* Notify institutions whose name is being used; they can act where the client cannot.
* Report the accounts under platform impersonation policy, which is enforced more reliably
  than misinformation policy.
data.short_recommendation: Verify claimed credentials with the institutions and notify them.
